questions.stem: What is total utility?

options.text: The satisfaction from the last unit consumed
The total satisfaction from consuming a certain quantity of goods
The additional satisfaction from consuming one more unit
The satisfaction from consuming goods over time

questions.explanation: Total utility refers to the overall satisfaction a consumer gets from consuming a certain quantity of goods or services. It is different from marginal utility, which is the satisfaction from the last unit consumed.

distractorRationale.a: This defines marginal utility, not total utility.
distractorRationale.c: This is a definition of marginal utility.
distractorRationale.d: This option incorrectly describes total utility as a time-based measure.

questions.stem: According to the law of diminishing marginal utility, what happens as a consumer consumes more units of a good?

options.text: Total utility decreases
Marginal utility increases
Marginal utility decreases
Total utility remains constant

questions.explanation: The law of diminishing marginal utility states that as more units of a good are consumed, the additional satisfaction (marginal utility) from each additional unit decreases.

distractorRationale.a: Total utility may still increase, but at a decreasing rate.
distractorRationale.d: Total utility does not remain constant; it increases at a decreasing rate.

questions.stem: What condition must be met for a consumer to be in equilibrium?

options.text: Total utility is maximized
Marginal utility per naira is equal for all goods
The consumer spends all their income
Marginal utility is zero

questions.explanation: Consumer equilibrium is achieved when the marginal utility per naira spent is equal across all goods, maximizing total utility given the budget constraint.

distractorRationale.a: While total utility is maximized, the condition specifically involves marginal utility per naira.
distractorRationale.c: Spending all income does not necessarily mean equilibrium is achieved.
distractorRationale.d: Marginal utility being zero is not a condition for equilibrium.

questions.stem: If a consumer finds that the marginal utility per naira spent on oranges is greater than that on bananas, what should they do to reach equilibrium?
